newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco inaugurates $1.4 bln gas pipeline section.
newsitem.headline: Morocco inaugurates $1.4 bln gas pipeline section.

text.p: Morocco on Monday inaugurated a $1.4 billion pipeline section with an annual capacity of 9.5 billion cubic metres of natural gas coming from Algeria's Hassi R'mel field to Spain via northern Morocco.

"This is a historical event which brought together our colleagues and neighbours, ministers of Algeria, Spain and Portugal, to inaugurate this station," said Moroccan Energy Minister Abdellatif Guerraoui.
Officials and reporters from the four countries attended the symbolic inauguration of a gas pumping station located on the Atlantic coast 10 km south of the northern city of Tangier.
Last month, Algeria inaugurated the first section of the Maghreb-Europe gas pipeline built at an estimated total cost of $2.4 billion over 30 months, officials said.

The gas pipeline, first envisaged in an agreement signed in 1991, runs from the Algerian gas field over a distance of 1,385 km, across Morocco, under the Strait of Gibraltar, to the Spanish city of Cordoba, and is to link up with a gas distribution network for Portugal.
Algeria hopes to double its present annual gas exports to 60 billion cubic metres by the year 2,000, when one Algerian official said its oil and gas exports should earn $16 billion.

Morocco later will use gas from Hassi R'mel, including for electricity generation, when it has created the necessary infrastructure. Until then it will take royalties as a share of the income generated, a Moroccan official said.
"A third inauguration ceremony is expected to take place in the Spanish city of Cordoba next week," the official said.
The pipeline section in Portugal is expected to be operational in January 1997.
